files.description: The review rules for this repository: path-scoped instructions, pre-merge checks, and the standards documents they rely on. .greptile/rules.md says how to apply them.
How work is done here: the publication boundary, commit rules, when a review is asked for, persisted shapes, crate layout.
Contribution rules: tests, changelog entries, documentation and pull request conventions.
The workspace's public description and its crate list.
Security policy and the handling of keys and secrets.
Who decides what, and how decisions are recorded.
The index of this repository's documentation.
Where a file goes and the numbered layout rules the tripwires enforce: tests in sibling files, errors in error.rs, file size limits.
The crate graph and the boundaries between crates.
What each crate is for.
The patterns this codebase uses and why.
The passport data model, envelope keys and product group data.
Why a change to a stored shape is a data-migration question: stored and fetched passports, the lens escape hatch, the signed public view.
How a product group schema version is added, and why a published version is never edited in place.
Lineage between passports, transfers of responsibility and the evidence behind them.
The Wasm plugin contract between host and guest.
The port traits at the boundary with the hosts that consume this workspace.
How dated obligations and their effective dates are modelled.
Identifiers, operators, keys and DIDs.
Which personal data may appear where, and how it is erased.
The standards register: every standard the code cites, its status and the evidence for each conformance claim.
The regulatory reading this repository has committed to, including why a rule module is a placeholder.
What the compliance checks decide, and on what basis in EU law.
Conformity with the standards and acts this workspace implements.
The pre-1.0 versioning rules, and the CHANGELOG convention: every breaking change under a Breaking heading with a migration note.
The release checklist.
Local development, the just recipes and the gates.
Branches, pull requests and how changes land on main.
The project's intended shape.
